references.text: The Israelites groaned under their slavery and cried out, and their cry went up to God. God heard their groaning and remembered his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God says that he has heard the cry of the Israelites whom the Egyptians hold in slavery, and he has remembered his covenant.
The angel of the Lord tells Hagar that the Lord has heard about her distress (עָנְיֵךְ), the same word used for the suffering of Israel.
Leah says that the Lord has seen her distress (עָנְיִי), the same expression God uses for seeing the suffering of Israel.
Moses reminds the people that they cried out to the Lord, and he heard their voice and saw their distress, slavery, and oppression.
Nehemiah confesses that God saw the distress of the ancestors in Egypt and heard their cry by the Red Sea.
The psalmist says that God looked upon them in their distress when he heard their cry.
In all their distress there was no distress for him, and the angel of the Lord saved them. In his love and compassion he redeemed them.
Stephen quotes this verse in his speech and says that God has seen the suffering of his people in Egypt, heard their groaning, and come down to deliver them.
Isaiah explicitly refers to this event to show that God's story of salvation is continuous.
